text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000319 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, mostly on patients with few or no chronic conditions, but the records sample is too thin to confirm or refute support.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, and most 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. That is not what a sicker panel looks like. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are often for minimal-complexity diagnoses: follow-up encounters (Z09, e.g. C0178035, C0178040), rash (R21, e.g. C0178123, C0178249), back pain (C0178017) and upper respiratory infection (C0178433). Documentation cannot settle the question. Only one documented 99215 came back. It was supported (C0178372), though it is a high-MDM, 47-minute rash visit for an 18-year-old with no chronic conditions, which is worth a closer look. The data-reviewed versus lab-line check shows almost no signal. Two points are ambiguous: the heavy 99214 volume may reflect a generally high-intensity practice style, and the modest plain peer z-score suggests some peers bill similarly. The reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, especially the Z09 and R21 visits. Enough documented 99215s are needed to compare the unsupported rate against the comparison providers' 9%."}
